properties.nhcTitle: East of the Leeward Islands (Remnants of Dolly)
properties.discussion:
A tropical wave, the remnants of Tropical Storm Dolly, are located  several hundred miles east of the Leeward Islands.  Redevelopment  of this system is unlikely while it moves westward to  west-northwestward near 25 mph.  The wave could bring locally heavy  rains and gusty winds to portions of the Leeward Islands, the  Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico over the next several days. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

properties.nhcTitle: Northeastern and North-Central Gulf of America
properties.discussion:
Disorganized cloudiness and showers over portions of the  northeastern and north-central Gulf of America are associated with  a weak area of low pressure.  Development, if any, of this system  is expected to be slow while it remains nearly stationary for the  next several days. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

An area of disturbed weather, associated with a tropical wave, is  located well to the south of southwestern Mexico. Environmental  conditions appear favorable for gradual development of this system,  and a tropical depression is likely to form early next week while  it moves west-northwestward to northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.  
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the  Hawaiian Islands in a few days. Some gradual development is possible  thereafter and a tropical depression could form during the middle  part of next week while the system moves slowly west-northwestward,  well offshore of the Hawaiian Islands. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.
